title: Osmotic pressure from independently placed particles
spoken: Pi equals R times T divided by N sub A, times the particle number density n.
explanation: Under the dilute independent-particle assumptions, differentiating the configurational free-energy difference gives pressure equal to the thermal energy per particle times the particle number density.
assumptions: The statistical free-energy relation and equilibrium pressure-work relation are admitted physical premises.
The particles are independent, dilute and uniformly placed, and the remaining configuration factor is independent of the confining volume.
Temperature and particle count are held fixed during the volume derivative. Temperature, volume, the reference volume, R and N are positive.
This is a modern teaching equation. Einstein writes p for pressure, nu for number density, and N for the number of molecules in a gram-molecule.

notes.title: The conditional osmotic law
notes.explanation: The equality follows from the statistical volume argument and the equilibrium work relation, under the stated dilution and independence assumptions.

notes.title: Osmotic pressure
notes.explanation: The pressure on the particle-confining wall, found as minus the free-energy derivative with respect to volume.

notes.title: Energy per particle times particles per volume
notes.explanation: Multiplying the thermal energy scale by number density gives energy per volume, the dimensions of pressure.

notes.title: From a mole to one particle
notes.explanation: Divide RT by Avogadro's constant. The amount dimension cancels and the result is an energy per particle.

notes.title: The molar thermal scale
notes.explanation: The gas constant multiplied by absolute temperature has energy-per-amount dimensions.

notes.title: The gas constant
notes.explanation: The molar gas constant R supplies the energy-per-amount-per-temperature scale.

notes.title: Absolute temperature held fixed
notes.explanation: Temperature is held fixed while the confining volume changes. Differentiating along a temperature change would be a different calculation.

notes.title: Avogadro's constant
notes.explanation: The number of particles per mole converts the molar thermal scale into a per-particle scale; it is not the number of suspended particles.

notes.title: Particles per volume
notes.explanation: Number density is total particle count divided by the accessible volume. It counts independent placements in the dilute model.
